deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N3::01 Voice and polite requests
text: (To a colleague) ちょっと{{c1::手伝ってもらえませんか::手伝う · could you? (polite)}}。
tr: Could you give me a hand?
notes: て-form + もらえませんか / いただけませんか: could you (please)? More polite than 〜てください; いただけませんか is the most polite.
tip: 〜てくれませんか is slightly less polite than もらえませんか.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N3::01 Voice and polite requests
text: (To your boss) この書類を{{c1::見ていただけませんか::見る · could you? (very polite)}}。
tr: Would you mind looking at this document?
notes: て-form + もらえませんか / いただけませんか: could you (please)? More polite than 〜てください; いただけませんか is the most polite.
tip: 〜てくれませんか is slightly less polite than もらえませんか.

text: (The lights are on) 田中さんはまだ会社に{{c1::いるに違いありません::いる · must be (I'm sure)}}。
tr: Mr Tanaka must still be at the office.
notes: Plain form + に違いない (nouns and な-adj drop だ): must be; I'm sure (strong conviction).
tip: vs はず: はず is based on reasoning or plans; に違いない is a personal conviction.

text: あの人が{{c1::犯人に違いありません::犯人 · must be}}。
tr: That person must be the culprit.
notes: Plain form + に違いない (nouns and な-adj drop だ): must be; I'm sure (strong conviction).
tip: vs はず: はず is based on reasoning or plans; に違いない is a personal conviction.

text: あんなにやさしい人がうそを{{c1::つくはずがありません::つく · there's no way}}。
tr: There's no way someone that kind would lie.
notes: Plain form + はずがない: there's no way; it can't be (based on reasons).
tip: Same meaning as わけがない.

text: (He's in Tokyo today) 田中さんが大阪に{{c1::いるはずがありません::いる · can't be}}。
tr: Mr Tanaka can't be in Osaka.
notes: Plain form + はずがない: there's no way; it can't be (based on reasons).
tip: Same meaning as わけがない.

text: 高い物がいつも{{c1::いいとは限りません::いい · not necessarily}}。
tr: Expensive things aren't necessarily good.
notes: Plain form + とは限らない: not necessarily; not always. Often used with いつも, みんな or 必ずしも.

text: 日本人がみんな漢字を{{c1::書けるとは限りません::書く · can, not necessarily}}。
tr: Not all Japanese people can write kanji.
notes: Plain form + とは限らない: not necessarily; not always. Often used with いつも, みんな or 必ずしも.

text:
(He's an adult) 彼は大人なのに、{{c1::子どもっぽい::っぽい or らしい?}}です。
(She's a child, in a good way) あの子はとても{{c2::子どもらしい::っぽい or らしい?}}です。
tr: He's an adult, but he's childish. / That kid is a real kid.
notes: っぽい: -ish; seems like (often negative or vague); after a verb stem, 'tends to' (忘れっぽい). Noun + らしい: a typical, proper example of that noun.
tip: N + みたい: looks like N but isn't.

text: 最近、{{c1::忘れっぽく::忘れる · tends to (っぽい)}}なりました。
tr: I've become forgetful lately.
notes: っぽい: -ish; seems like (often negative or vague); after a verb stem, 'tends to' (忘れっぽい). Noun + らしい: a typical, proper example of that noun.
tip: N + みたい: looks like N but isn't.

text: (To a friend) このシャツ、ちょっと{{c1::安っぽい::安い · cheap-looking (っぽい)}}ね。
tr: This shirt looks a bit cheap.
notes: っぽい: -ish; seems like (often negative or vague); after a verb stem, 'tends to' (忘れっぽい). Noun + らしい: a typical, proper example of that noun.
tip: N + みたい: looks like N but isn't.

text: (He lived in Japan for ten years) 日本語が上手な{{c1::わけです::わけです / わけではありません / わけにはいきません / わけがありません}}。
tr: No wonder his Japanese is good.
notes: わけです: that's why; no wonder (a logical conclusion). わけではありません: it's not that… (partial denial). わけにはいきません: can't (for social or moral reasons). わけがありません: there's no way.

text: 肉がきらいな{{c1::わけではありません::わけです / わけではありません / わけにはいきません / わけがありません}}が、あまり食べません。
tr: It's not that I dislike meat, but I don't eat it much.
notes: わけです: that's why; no wonder (a logical conclusion). わけではありません: it's not that… (partial denial). わけにはいきません: can't (for social or moral reasons). わけがありません: there's no way.

text: 明日は大事な会議があるので、休む{{c1::わけにはいきません::わけです / わけではありません / わけにはいきません / わけがありません}}。
tr: I've got an important meeting tomorrow, so I can't take the day off.
notes: わけです: that's why; no wonder (a logical conclusion). わけではありません: it's not that… (partial denial). わけにはいきません: can't (for social or moral reasons). わけがありません: there's no way.

text: (He's never studied) 彼にこの問題がわかる{{c1::わけがありません::わけです / わけではありません / わけにはいきません / わけがありません}}。
tr: There's no way he can understand this question.
notes: わけです: that's why; no wonder (a logical conclusion). わけではありません: it's not that… (partial denial). わけにはいきません: can't (for social or moral reasons). わけがありません: there's no way.

text: {{c1::若いうちに::若い · while (before it changes)}}、いろいろな国へ行きたいです。
tr: I want to go to lots of countries while I'm young.
notes: うちに: while (a state lasts), do it before it changes. ないうちに: before something happens. Also 'while doing (without noticing, a change happened)'.
tip: vs あいだに: neutral 'during'; うちに implies 'before it's too late'.

text: 雨が{{c1::ふらないうちに::ふる · before (it happens)}}、帰りましょう。
tr: Let's go home before it rains.
notes: うちに: while (a state lasts), do it before it changes. ないうちに: before something happens. Also 'while doing (without noticing, a change happened)'.
tip: vs あいだに: neutral 'during'; うちに implies 'before it's too late'.

text: 日本に住んでいる{{c1::うちに::while (gradually)}}、日本語が上手になりました。
tr: While living in Japan, my Japanese got better.
notes: うちに: while (a state lasts), do it before it changes. ないうちに: before something happens. Also 'while doing (without noticing, a change happened)'.
tip: vs あいだに: neutral 'during'; うちに implies 'before it's too late'.

text:
夏休みの{{c1::あいだ::あいだ or あいだに?}}、ずっと国に帰っていました。
母がねている{{c2::あいだに::あいだ or あいだに?}}、そうじをしました。
tr: I was back home for the whole summer holidays. / I cleaned while my mother was asleep.
notes: あいだ: throughout the whole time (a continuous action). あいだに: at some point during that time.

text: {{c1::立ち上がったとたん::立ち上がる · the moment}}、めまいがしました。
tr: The moment I stood up, I felt dizzy.
notes: Past た + とたん(に): the moment A happened, B (unexpected). B can't be a request or your own intention.

text: ドアを{{c1::あけたとたん::あける · the moment}}、ねこが外に飛び出しました。
tr: The moment I opened the door, the cat ran outside.
notes: Past た + とたん(に): the moment A happened, B (unexpected). B can't be a request or your own intention.

text: 会議の{{c1::最中に::right in the middle of}}、電話が鳴りました。
tr: The phone rang right in the middle of the meeting.
notes: Noun + の / ている + 最中に: right in the middle of (and then something interrupts).

text: 食事を{{c1::している最中に::する · in the middle of}}、地震がありました。
tr: There was an earthquake right in the middle of our meal.
notes: Noun + の / ている + 最中に: right in the middle of (and then something interrupts).

text:
(You haven't left yet) 今から{{c1::出かけるところです::出かける · about to / doing / just did}}。
(Eating right now) 今、ごはんを{{c2::食べているところです::食べる · about to / doing / just did}}。
(Got home a moment ago) 今、うちに{{c3::帰ったところです::帰る · about to / doing / just did}}。
tr: I'm just about to go out. / I'm in the middle of eating. / I've just got home.
notes: Dictionary form + ところ: about to. ているところ: in the middle of. たところ: just did.
tip: vs たばかり: たばかり feels recent but can be days or months ago.

text: 先月、日本に{{c1::来たばかりです::来る · only recently}}。
tr: I only came to Japan last month.
notes: Past た + ばかり: just did; only recently (it feels recent to the speaker, even weeks or months ago).
tip: vs たところ: たところ is only for the moment right after.

text: {{c1::買ったばかり::買う · only just}}なのに、もうこわれました。
tr: I only just bought it, and it's already broken.
notes: Past た + ばかり: just did; only recently (it feels recent to the speaker, even weeks or months ago).
tip: vs たところ: たところ is only for the moment right after.

text: この歌を{{c1::聞くたびに::聞く · every time}}、国を思い出します。
tr: Every time I hear this song, I think of home.
notes: Dictionary form / noun + の + たびに: every time.

text: 旅行の{{c1::たびに::every time}}、おみやげを買います。
tr: I buy souvenirs every time I travel.
notes: Dictionary form / noun + の + たびに: every time.

text: 年を{{c1::とるにつれて::とる · as (gradually)}}、体が弱くなります。
tr: As you get older, your body gets weaker.
notes: Dictionary form / noun + につれて: as A changes, B changes too (gradual, in step).
tip: にしたがって means the same and is slightly more formal.

text: 時間がたつ{{c1::につれて::as (gradually)}}、町は変わっていきました。
tr: As time went by, the town changed.
notes: Dictionary form / noun + につれて: as A changes, B changes too (gradual, in step).
tip: にしたがって means the same and is slightly more formal.

text: 買い物の{{c1::ついでに::while (at it)}}、銀行に行きました。
tr: While I was out shopping, I went to the bank.
notes: Dictionary form / past / noun + の + ついでに: while you're at it; taking the opportunity.

text: 駅へ{{c1::行くついでに::行く · while (at it)}}、手紙を出してきます。
tr: While I'm going to the station, I'll post a letter.
notes: Dictionary form / past / noun + の + ついでに: while you're at it; taking the opportunity.

text: 雨が{{c1::ふっても::ふる · even if}}、行きます。
tr: Even if it rains, I'll go.
notes: て-form + も (noun / な-adj + でも): even if. たとえ adds emphasis. Question word + ても: no matter what / how.
tip: vs のに: のに is about something that has actually happened.

text: たとえ{{c1::高くても::高い · even if}}、買います。
tr: Even if it's expensive, I'll buy it.
notes: て-form + も (noun / な-adj + でも): even if. たとえ adds emphasis. Question word + ても: no matter what / how.
tip: vs のに: のに is about something that has actually happened.

text: いくら{{c1::勉強しても::勉強する · no matter how much}}、覚えられません。
tr: No matter how much I study, I can't remember it.
notes: て-form + も (noun / な-adj + でも): even if. たとえ adds emphasis. Question word + ても: no matter what / how.
tip: vs のに: のに is about something that has actually happened.

text: 何を{{c1::言っても::言う · no matter what}}、彼は聞きません。
tr: Whatever you say, he won't listen.
notes: て-form + も (noun / な-adj + でも): even if. たとえ adds emphasis. Question word + ても: no matter what / how.
tip: vs のに: のに is about something that has actually happened.

text: もし宝くじが{{c1::当たったとしたら::当たる · supposing}}、何をしますか。
tr: Supposing you won the lottery, what would you do?
notes: Plain form + としたら / とすれば: supposing that; if (purely hypothetical).
tip: vs たら: たら can be a real future event; としたら stresses 'just suppose'.

text: もし生まれ変わる{{c1::としたら::supposing}}、何になりたいですか。
tr: If you were reborn, what would you want to be?
notes: Plain form + としたら / とすれば: supposing that; if (purely hypothetical).
tip: vs たら: たら can be a real future event; としたら stresses 'just suppose'.

text: 練習すれば{{c1::するほど::する · the more}}、上手になります。
tr: The more you practise, the better you get.
notes: ば-form + the same word in dictionary form + ほど: the more A, the more B.

text: 日本語は{{c1::勉強すれば::勉強する · the more (ば)}}するほど、おもしろくなります。
tr: The more you study Japanese, the more interesting it gets.
notes: ば-form + the same word in dictionary form + ほど: the more A, the more B.

text: 考えれば{{c1::考えるほど::考える · the more}}、わからなくなります。
tr: The more I think about it, the less I understand.
notes: ば-form + the same word in dictionary form + ほど: the more A, the more B.

text: 安ければ{{c1::安いほど::安い · the more}}いいです。
tr: The cheaper the better.
notes: ば-form + the same word in dictionary form + ほど: the more A, the more B.

text: お金{{c1::さえ::as long as (only)}}あれば、何でも買えます。
tr: As long as you have money, you can buy anything.
notes: Noun + さえ + ば-form: if only; as long as (that's all it takes). With verbs: stem + さえすれば.

text: この薬を{{c1::飲みさえすれば::飲む · as long as you just}}、すぐよくなります。
tr: As long as you take this medicine, you'll soon get better.
notes: Noun + さえ + ば-form: if only; as long as (that's all it takes). With verbs: stem + さえすれば.

text: (To a friend) 知っている{{c1::くせに::even though (criticising)}}、教えてくれない。
tr: You know, but you won't tell me.
notes: Plain form + くせに (noun + の, な-adj + な): even though (criticising someone). Stronger than のに; not used about yourself.
tip: vs のに: のに shows disappointment but can be neutral or about yourself.

text: (To a friend) 彼は{{c1::下手なくせに::下手 · even though (criticising)}}、いつも歌いたがる。
tr: He's bad at it, but he always wants to sing.
notes: Plain form + くせに (noun + の, な-adj + な): even though (criticising someone). Stronger than のに; not used about yourself.
tip: vs のに: のに shows disappointment but can be neutral or about yourself.

text: この店は値段の{{c1::わりに::considering}}おいしいです。
tr: Considering the price, the food here is good.
notes: Plain form / noun + の + わりに: considering (the result is better or worse than you'd expect). Noun + にしては: for (a specific case; unexpectedly).
tip: わりに works with words of degree (値段, 年); にしては with a specific standard (初めて, 日曜日).

text: 彼は{{c1::年のわりに::年 · considering}}若く見えます。
tr: He looks young for his age.
notes: Plain form / noun + の + わりに: considering (the result is better or worse than you'd expect). Noun + にしては: for (a specific case; unexpectedly).
tip: わりに works with words of degree (値段, 年); にしては with a specific standard (初めて, 日曜日).

text: 初めて{{c1::にしては::for (a specific case)}}、上手ですね。
tr: That's good for a first try.
notes: Plain form / noun + の + わりに: considering (the result is better or worse than you'd expect). Noun + にしては: for (a specific case; unexpectedly).
tip: わりに works with words of degree (値段, 年); にしては with a specific standard (初めて, 日曜日).

text: 日曜日{{c1::にしては::for (a specific case)}}、すいていますね。
tr: It's quiet for a Sunday.
notes: Plain form / noun + の + わりに: considering (the result is better or worse than you'd expect). Noun + にしては: for (a specific case; unexpectedly).
tip: わりに works with words of degree (値段, 年); にしては with a specific standard (初めて, 日曜日).

text:
日本の歴史{{c1::について::について / に対して / にとって}}調べています。
先生は学生{{c2::に対して::について / に対して / にとって}}とてもきびしいです。
私{{c3::にとって::について / に対して / にとって}}、家族がいちばん大切です。
tr: I'm researching Japanese history. / The teacher is very strict with the students. / For me, family is the most important thing.
notes: について: about (a topic). に対して: towards, against (the target of an attitude or action); also 'in contrast to'. にとって: for; from the point of view of (followed by a judgement).

text: 国{{c1::によって::depending on}}、習慣がちがいます。
tr: Customs differ from country to country.
notes: Noun + によって: (a) depending on; (b) by (the creator, in passive sentences); (c) by means of. による + noun. によると: according to.

text: この本は有名な作家{{c1::によって::by (creator)}}書かれました。
tr: This book was written by a famous author.
notes: Noun + によって: (a) depending on; (b) by (the creator, in passive sentences); (c) by means of. による + noun. によると: according to.

text: 地震{{c1::による::caused by (before a noun)}}被害は大きかったです。
tr: The damage caused by the earthquake was severe.
notes: Noun + によって: (a) depending on; (b) by (the creator, in passive sentences); (c) by means of. による + noun. によると: according to.

text: ニュース{{c1::によると::according to}}、明日は雪だそうです。
tr: According to the news, it will snow tomorrow.
notes: Noun + によって: (a) depending on; (b) by (the creator, in passive sentences); (c) by means of. による + noun. によると: according to.

text: 留学生{{c1::として::as (role)}}日本に来ました。
tr: I came to Japan as an international student.
notes: Noun + として: as (in the role or capacity of).

text: 趣味{{c1::として::as}}ピアノをひいています。
tr: I play the piano as a hobby.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::01 Casual speech, quoting and explaining
text:
(TV weather forecast) 明日は雨{{c1::でしょう::でしょう or だろう?}}。
(In your diary) 明日はたぶん雨{{c2::だろう::でしょう or だろう?}}。
tr: It will probably rain tomorrow. / It'll probably rain tomorrow.
notes: だろう is the plain form of でしょう ('probably'). Use it in casual speech, thinking to yourself, and writing.
tip: でしょう = polite; だろう = plain.
register: でしょう polite / だろう casual or written

text: 私は漢字が{{c1::読めます::読む · can}}。
tr: I can read kanji.
notes: う-verb: change the final u to e + る (読む → 読める). る-verb: られる (食べられる). する → できる. 来る → 来られる. The object often takes が.
tip: In speech, ら is often dropped (来れる, 食べれる); textbooks and exams use the full form.

text: 田中さんはさしみが{{c1::食べられません::食べる · can't}}。
tr: Mr Tanaka can't eat sashimi.
notes: う-verb: change the final u to e + る (読む → 読める). る-verb: られる (食べられる). する → できる. 来る → 来られる. The object often takes が.
tip: In speech, ら is often dropped (来れる, 食べれる); textbooks and exams use the full form.

text: 日本語が少し{{c1::話せます::話す · can}}。
tr: I can speak a little Japanese.
notes: う-verb: change the final u to e + る (読む → 読める). る-verb: られる (食べられる). する → できる. 来る → 来られる. The object often takes が.
tip: In speech, ら is often dropped (来れる, 食べれる); textbooks and exams use the full form.

text: 明日は{{c1::来られますか::来る · can? (question)}}。
tr: Can you come tomorrow?
notes: う-verb: change the final u to e + る (読む → 読める). る-verb: られる (食べられる). する → できる. 来る → 来られる. The object often takes が.
tip: In speech, ら is often dropped (来れる, 食べれる); textbooks and exams use the full form.

text: 私は{{c1::およげません::およぐ · can't}}。
tr: I can't swim.
notes: う-verb: change the final u to e + る (読む → 読める). る-verb: られる (食べられる). する → できる. 来る → 来られる. The object often takes が.
tip: In speech, ら is often dropped (来れる, 食べれる); textbooks and exams use the full form.

text: ここでカードを{{c1::使うことができます::使う · can (ことができる)}}。
tr: You can use a card here.
notes: Dictionary form + ことができる: can. Same meaning as the potential form, but more formal.
tip: vs potential form: more common in speech.

text: 私はピアノを{{c1::ひくことができます::ひく · can (ことができる)}}。
tr: I can play the piano.
notes: Dictionary form + ことができる: can. Same meaning as the potential form, but more formal.
tip: vs potential form: more common in speech.

text:
(Out of the window) 山が{{c1::見えます::見えます or 見られます?}}。
(On a streaming site) この映画はインターネットで{{c2::見られます::見えます or 見られます?}}。
tr: You can see the mountains. / You can watch this film online.
notes: 見える / 聞こえる: something is visible or audible without effort. 見られる / 聞ける: you are able to see or hear it (you have access or the chance).

text:
(Through the wall) となりのへやから音楽が{{c1::聞こえます::聞こえます or 聞けます?}}。
(With this app) このアプリで音楽が{{c2::聞けます::聞こえます or 聞けます?}}。
tr: I can hear music from the next room. / You can listen to music with this app.
notes: 見える / 聞こえる: something is visible or audible without effort. 見られる / 聞ける: you are able to see or hear it (you have access or the chance).

text: 雨が{{c1::ふったら::ふる · たら}}、行きません。
tr: If it rains, I won't go.
notes: Plain past + ら: if / when (once A happens, then B). The most general conditional; B can be a request, wish or plan.
tip: vs ば and と: those usually can't be followed by a request when A is an action.

text: 駅に{{c1::ついたら::つく · たら}}、電話してください。
tr: When you get to the station, please call me.
notes: Plain past + ら: if / when (once A happens, then B). The most general conditional; B can be a request, wish or plan.
tip: vs ば and と: those usually can't be followed by a request when A is an action.

text: お金が{{c1::あったら::ある · たら}}、車を買います。
tr: If I have the money, I'll buy a car.
notes: Plain past + ら: if / when (once A happens, then B). The most general conditional; B can be a request, wish or plan.
tip: vs ば and と: those usually can't be followed by a request when A is an action.

text: {{c1::安かったら::安い · たら}}、買います。
tr: If it's cheap, I'll buy it.
notes: Plain past + ら: if / when (once A happens, then B). The most general conditional; B can be a request, wish or plan.
tip: vs ば and と: those usually can't be followed by a request when A is an action.

text: 春に{{c1::なれば::なる · ば}}、あたたかくなります。
tr: When spring comes, it gets warm.
notes: う-verb: change the final u to e + ば (飲む → 飲めば). る-verb: れば. い-adj: ければ (いい → よければ). Noun / な-adj: なら. Focus is on the condition itself: 'if (only) A, then B'.
tip: vs たら: ば is more general and hypothetical; it sounds odd before a request or a past fact.

text: この薬を{{c1::飲めば::飲む · ば}}、よくなります。
tr: If you take this medicine, you'll get better.
notes: う-verb: change the final u to e + ば (飲む → 飲めば). る-verb: れば. い-adj: ければ (いい → よければ). Noun / な-adj: なら. Focus is on the condition itself: 'if (only) A, then B'.
tip: vs たら: ば is more general and hypothetical; it sounds odd before a request or a past fact.

text: 時間が{{c1::あれば::ある · ば}}、行きます。
tr: If I have time, I'll go.
notes: う-verb: change the final u to e + ば (飲む → 飲めば). る-verb: れば. い-adj: ければ (いい → よければ). Noun / な-adj: なら. Focus is on the condition itself: 'if (only) A, then B'.
tip: vs たら: ば is more general and hypothetical; it sounds odd before a request or a past fact.

text: {{c1::高ければ::高い · ば}}、買いません。
tr: If it's expensive, I won't buy it.
notes: う-verb: change the final u to e + ば (飲む → 飲めば). る-verb: れば. い-adj: ければ (いい → よければ). Noun / な-adj: なら. Focus is on the condition itself: 'if (only) A, then B'.
tip: vs たら: ば is more general and hypothetical; it sounds odd before a request or a past fact.

text: このボタンを{{c1::おすと::おす · と (whenever)}}、ドアがあきます。
tr: When you press this button, the door opens.
notes: Dictionary form + と: whenever A, B (always or automatically). B can't be a request, invitation or intention.
tip: vs たら: たら works for one-off events and requests.

text: 春に{{c1::なると::なる · と (whenever)}}、さくらがさきます。
tr: When spring comes, the cherry blossoms bloom.
notes: Dictionary form + と: whenever A, B (always or automatically). B can't be a request, invitation or intention.
tip: vs たら: たら works for one-off events and requests.

text: 右に{{c1::まがると::まがる · と}}、駅があります。
tr: Turn right and you'll find the station.
notes: Dictionary form + と: whenever A, B (always or automatically). B can't be a request, invitation or intention.
tip: vs たら: たら works for one-off events and requests.

text: (Friend: 'I'm going to Kyoto.') 京都へ{{c1::行くなら::行く · なら}}、新幹線が便利です。
tr: If you're going to Kyoto, the bullet train is convenient.
notes: Noun / plain form + なら: if it's the case that X; as for X. Often a reply to what someone has just said. The advice in B can happen before A.
tip: vs たら: たら means after A has happened.

text: (Asked about sushi) すし{{c1::なら::particle: if it's / as for}}、あの店がおいしいです。
tr: If it's sushi you want, that place is good.
notes: Noun / plain form + なら: if it's the case that X; as for X. Often a reply to what someone has just said. The advice in B can happen before A.
tip: vs たら: たら means after A has happened.

text:
(Call me after you arrive) 駅に{{c1::ついたら::つく · たら or なら?}}、電話してください。
(Advice before the trip) 京都へ{{c2::行くなら::行く · たら or なら?}}、新幹線が便利です。
tr: When you get to the station, call me. / If you're going to Kyoto, the bullet train is convenient.
notes: たら: B happens after A. なら: B is advice given before A happens.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: (To a friend) いっしょに{{c1::帰ろう::帰る · let's (casual)}}。
tr: Let's go home together.
notes: う-verb: change the final u to o + う (行く → 行こう). る-verb: よう (食べよう). する → しよう. 来る → 来よう (こよう). Casual equivalent of 〜ましょう.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: (To a friend) 何を{{c1::食べようか::食べる · shall we? (casual)}}。
tr: What shall we eat?
notes: う-verb: change the final u to o + う (行く → 行こう). る-verb: よう (食べよう). する → しよう. 来る → 来よう (こよう). Casual equivalent of 〜ましょう.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: (To a friend) 少し{{c1::休もう::休む · let's (casual)}}。
tr: Let's take a little break.
notes: う-verb: change the final u to o + う (行く → 行こう). る-verb: よう (食べよう). する → しよう. 来る → 来よう (こよう). Casual equivalent of 〜ましょう.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: 夏休みに日本へ{{c1::行こうと思っています::行く · I'm thinking of (ongoing)}}。
tr: I'm thinking of going to Japan in the summer holidays.
notes: Volitional + と思っています / と思います: I'm thinking of doing; I intend to (often still being considered).
tip: vs つもり: つもり is a firmer plan.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: 来年、車を{{c1::買おうと思います::買う · I think I'll}}。
tr: I think I'll buy a car next year.
notes: Volitional + と思っています / と思います: I'm thinking of doing; I intend to (often still being considered).
tip: vs つもり: つもり is a firmer plan.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: 来年、日本へ{{c1::行くつもりです::行く · intend to}}。
tr: I intend to go to Japan next year.
notes: Dictionary form + つもりです: intend to; plan to. ない + つもり: intend not to.
tip: vs ようと思う: つもり is firmer. Asking a superior 'つもりですか' can sound rude.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: もうたばこは{{c1::すわないつもりです::すう · intend not to}}。
tr: I intend not to smoke any more.
notes: Dictionary form + つもりです: intend to; plan to. ない + つもり: intend not to.
tip: vs ようと思う: つもり is firmer. Asking a superior 'つもりですか' can sound rude.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: 会議は三時に{{c1::始まる予定です::始まる · scheduled}}。
tr: The meeting is scheduled to start at three.
notes: Dictionary form / noun + の + 予定です: it is scheduled (an arrangement already made, not just an intention).
tip: vs つもり: つもり = intention; 予定 = schedule.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: 来週は{{c1::旅行の予定です::旅行 · scheduled}}。
tr: I have a trip scheduled for next week.
notes: Dictionary form / noun + の + 予定です: it is scheduled (an arrangement already made, not just an intention).
tip: vs つもり: つもり = intention; 予定 = schedule.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text:
(Your own choice) 毎朝走る{{c1::ことにしました::ことにする or ことになる? (past)}}。
(Your company decided) 来月から大阪で働く{{c2::ことになりました::ことにする or ことになる? (past)}}。
tr: I've decided to run every morning. / It's been decided that I'll work in Osaka from next month.
notes: ことにする: I decide (my own choice). ことになる: it has been decided (by others or by circumstances).
register: Neutral; ことになる is common in formal announcements

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: (Your own choice) 今日から日本語で日記を書く{{c1::ことにしました::ことにする or ことになる? (past)}}。
tr: I've decided to keep a diary in Japanese from today.
notes: ことにする: I decide (my own choice). ことになる: it has been decided (by others or by circumstances).
register: Neutral; ことになる is common in formal announcements

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: 日本語が{{c1::話せるようになりました::話す · came to be able to}}。
tr: I've become able to speak Japanese.
notes: Dictionary / potential form + ようになる: come to (be able to) do. A gradual change in ability or habit.
tip: vs ことになる: that is a decision, not a gradual change.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: 毎日野菜を{{c1::食べるようになりました::食べる · came to (habit)}}。
tr: I've started eating vegetables every day.
notes: Dictionary / potential form + ようになる: come to (be able to) do. A gradual change in ability or habit.
tip: vs ことになる: that is a decision, not a gradual change.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: 毎日早く{{c1::ねるようにしています::ねる · make a point of}}。
tr: I make a point of going to bed early every day.
notes: Dictionary / ない form + ようにしています: make a point of; try to (as a habit).
tip: vs ようになる: ようにする = your own effort; ようになる = a change that happens.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N4::04 Intention, decisions and change
text: あまいものを{{c1::食べないようにしています::食べる · try not to}}。
tr: I try not to eat sweet things.
notes: Dictionary / ない form + ようにしています: make a point of; try to (as a habit).
tip: vs ようになる: ようにする = your own effort; ようになる = a change that happens.

text: 宿題をぜんぶ{{c1::やってしまいました::やる · completely (てしまう)}}。
tr: I've finished all my homework.
notes: て-form + しまう: (a) do completely; (b) do by accident or with regret. Casual: 〜ちゃう / 〜じゃう.

text: さいふを{{c1::なくしてしまいました::なくす · regret / accident}}。
tr: I've lost my wallet.
notes: て-form + しまう: (a) do completely; (b) do by accident or with regret. Casual: 〜ちゃう / 〜じゃう.

text: (To a friend) ケーキをぜんぶ{{c1::食べちゃった::食べる · casual てしまう, past}}。
tr: I ate the whole cake (oops).
notes: て-form + しまう: (a) do completely; (b) do by accident or with regret. Casual: 〜ちゃう / 〜じゃう.

text: パーティーの前に飲み物を{{c1::買っておきます::買う · in advance}}。
tr: I'll buy drinks before the party.
notes: て-form + おく: (a) do in advance, to prepare; (b) leave something as it is. Casual: 〜とく.

text: 旅行の前にホテルを{{c1::予約しておきました::予約する · in advance}}。
tr: I booked a hotel before the trip.
notes: て-form + おく: (a) do in advance, to prepare; (b) leave something as it is. Casual: 〜とく.

text: まどは{{c1::あけておいてください::あける · leave as is (request)}}。
tr: Please leave the window open.
notes: て-form + おく: (a) do in advance, to prepare; (b) leave something as it is. Casual: 〜とく.

text: 一度すしを{{c1::食べてみたいです::食べる · want to try}}。
tr: I'd like to try sushi once.
notes: て-form + みる: try doing (to see what it's like).

text: この服を{{c1::着てみます::着る · try}}。
tr: I'll try these clothes on.
notes: て-form + みる: try doing (to see what it's like).

text: 新しい店に{{c1::行ってみました::行く · tried (to see)}}。
tr: I tried the new shop.
notes: て-form + みる: try doing (to see what it's like).

text:
(Someone opened it on purpose) まどが{{c1::あけてあります::あけてあります or あいています?}}。
(It's just open) まどが{{c2::あいています::あけてあります or あいています?}}。
tr: The window has been opened (on purpose). / The window is open.
notes: Transitive verb + てある: someone did it on purpose and the result remains (often as preparation). Intransitive verb + ている: a state, with no one implied.
tip: Transitive + ている (まどをあけている) = someone is opening it right now.

text: かべにカレンダーが{{c1::はってあります::はる · てある}}。
tr: A calendar has been put up on the wall.
notes: Transitive verb + てある: someone did it on purpose and the result remains (often as preparation). Intransitive verb + ている: a state, with no one implied.
tip: Transitive + ている (まどをあけている) = someone is opening it right now.

text: つくえの上にメモが{{c1::おいてあります::おく · てある}}。
tr: A note has been left on the desk.
notes: Transitive verb + てある: someone did it on purpose and the result remains (often as preparation). Intransitive verb + ている: a state, with no one implied.
tip: Transitive + ている (まどをあけている) = someone is opening it right now.

text:
(From now on) これから寒くなって{{c1::いきます::いく or くる?}}。
(Up to now) 最近、日本語がおもしろくなって{{c2::きました::いく or くる?}}。
tr: It's going to keep getting colder from now on. / Japanese has been getting more interesting lately.
notes: てくる: a change up to now, or 'go and do, then come back'. ていく: a change from now on, into the future.

text: コンビニで飲み物を{{c1::買ってきます::買う · go and come back}}。
tr: I'll pop to the shop and buy some drinks.
notes: てくる: a change up to now, or 'go and do, then come back'. ていく: a change from now on, into the future.

text: 明日は{{c1::来なくてもいいです::来る · don't have to}}。
tr: You don't have to come tomorrow.

tip: vs なければならない: must.

text: くつを{{c1::ぬがなくてもいいです::ぬぐ · don't have to}}。
tr: You don't have to take your shoes off.
notes: ない form: drop い, add くてもいい: don't have to.
tip: vs なければならない: must.

text: 明日は早く{{c1::起きなければなりません::起きる · must}}。
tr: I have to get up early tomorrow.
notes: ない form: drop い, add ければなりません / くてはいけません: must. Casual: 〜なきゃ / 〜なくちゃ.
tip: vs てはいけない (N5): must not.

text: この薬を{{c1::飲まなければなりません::飲む · must}}。
tr: I have to take this medicine.
notes: ない form: drop い, add ければなりません / くてはいけません: must. Casual: 〜なきゃ / 〜なくちゃ.
tip: vs てはいけない (N5): must not.

text: (To a friend) もう{{c1::帰らなきゃ::帰る · must (casual)}}。
tr: I've got to go home now.
notes: ない form: drop い, add ければなりません / くてはいけません: must. Casual: 〜なきゃ / 〜なくちゃ.
tip: vs てはいけない (N5): must not.

text: 薬を{{c1::飲んだほうがいいです::飲む · you'd better}}。

text: あまりお酒を{{c1::飲まないほうがいいです::飲む · better not}}。

notes: Past た + ほうがいい: you'd better (advice). ない + ほうがいい: you'd better not.
tip: Dictionary form + ほうがいい also exists but sounds more general.
register: Neutral; can sound pushy to superiors

text: 母に{{c1::来てほしいです::来る · want (someone) to}}。
tr: I want my mother to come.
notes: Person に + て-form + ほしい: want someone to do something.
tip: vs たい: what you want to do yourself.

text: 友だちにもっと{{c1::話してほしいです::話す · want (someone) to}}。
tr: I want my friend to talk more.
notes: Person に + て-form + ほしい: want someone to do something.
tip: vs たい: what you want to do yourself.

text:
私は友だちに本を{{c1::あげました::あげる / くれる / もらう}}。
友だちは私に本を{{c2::くれました::あげる / くれる / もらう}}。

notes: Stem + たい: 'want to do'. Inflects like an い-adjective (たくない, たかった). Use for yourself, or in questions to the listener.
tip: vs ほしい: ほしい = want a noun. For a third person you need 〜たがる (N4).
register: Don't state a third person's wants directly

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::03 Polite verbs, wants and invitations
text: 私は新しい車が{{c1::ほしいです::want}}。
tr: I want a new car.
notes: Noun が ほしい: want a thing. Stem + たい: want to do an action.
tip: ほしい = noun; たい = verb.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::03 Polite verbs, wants and invitations
text: 私は犬が{{c1::ほしいです::want}}。
tr: I want a dog.
notes: Noun が ほしい: want a thing. Stem + たい: want to do an action.
tip: ほしい = noun; たい = verb.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::03 Polite verbs, wants and invitations
text:
車が{{c1::ほしい::want}}です。
日本に{{c2::行きたい::行く · want to}}です。
tr: I want a car. / I want to go to Japan.
notes: Noun が ほしい: want a thing. Stem + たい: want to do an action.
tip: ほしい = noun; たい = verb.

text: 毎日水{{c1::を::particle: object}}飲みます。
tr: I drink water every day.
notes: を marks the direct object (read 'o').
tip: vs が: を with action verbs; が with すき/ほしい/じょうず etc. (unit 05).

text: 私は本{{c1::を::particle: object}}読みます。
tr: I read a book.
notes: を marks the direct object (read 'o').
tip: vs が: を with action verbs; が with すき/ほしい/じょうず etc. (unit 05).

text: 朝ごはん{{c1::を::particle: object}}食べます。
tr: I eat breakfast.
notes: を marks the direct object (read 'o').
tip: vs が: を with action verbs; が with すき/ほしい/じょうず etc. (unit 05).

text: 友だち{{c1::を::particle: object}}待ちます。
tr: I wait for my friend.
notes: を marks the direct object (read 'o').
tip: vs が: を with action verbs; が with すき/ほしい/じょうず etc. (unit 05).

text: 学校{{c1::で::で or に?}}日本語を話します。
tr: I speak Japanese at school.
notes: で marks where an action happens.
tip: vs に: に = where something exists, or where you go.

text: うち{{c1::で::で or に?}}ごはんを食べます。
tr: I eat at home.
notes: で marks where an action happens.
tip: vs に: に = where something exists, or where you go.

text: デパート{{c1::で::で or に?}}くつを買います。
tr: I buy shoes at the department store.
notes: で marks where an action happens.
tip: vs に: に = where something exists, or where you go.

text: はし{{c1::で::で or と?}}食べます。
tr: I eat with chopsticks.
notes: で marks the means: tool, transport, language.
tip: vs と: と = together with a person.

text: バス{{c1::で::で or と?}}学校へ行きます。
tr: I go to school by bus.
notes: で marks the means: tool, transport, language.
tip: vs と: と = together with a person.

text: 日本語{{c1::で::で or と?}}手紙を書きます。
tr: I write letters in Japanese.
notes: で marks the means: tool, transport, language.
tip: vs と: と = together with a person.

text: 七時{{c1::に::particle: at (time)}}起きます。
tr: I get up at seven.
notes: に marks a specific point in time: clock times, days of the week, dates, months.
tip: No に after relative time words: 今日, 明日, 昨日, 毎日, 今.

text: 日曜日{{c1::に::particle: on (day)}}友だちに会います。
tr: I meet a friend on Sunday.
notes: に marks a specific point in time: clock times, days of the week, dates, months.
tip: No に after relative time words: 今日, 明日, 昨日, 毎日, 今.

text: 十月{{c1::に::particle: in (month)}}日本へ行きます。
tr: I'm going to Japan in October.
notes: に marks a specific point in time: clock times, days of the week, dates, months.
tip: No に after relative time words: 今日, 明日, 昨日, 毎日, 今.

text:
友だちは学校{{c1::に::に or で?}}行きます。
私は学校{{c2::で::に or で?}}日本語を話します。
ねこは学校{{c3::に::に or で?}}います。
tr: My friend goes to school. / I speak Japanese at school. / There's a cat at the school.
notes: に/へ mark the destination (へ is read 'e'). に also marks the person you meet (友だちに会う) and where something exists.
tip: vs で: で = place where an action happens.

text: 日本{{c1::へ::particle: towards (not に)}}行きます。
tr: I go to Japan.
notes: に/へ mark the destination (へ is read 'e'). に also marks the person you meet (友だちに会う) and where something exists.
tip: vs で: で = place where an action happens.

text: 毎日友だち{{c1::に::に or を?}}会います。
tr: I meet my friend every day.
notes: に/へ mark the destination (へ is read 'e'). に also marks the person you meet (友だちに会う) and where something exists.
tip: vs で: で = place where an action happens.

text: 九時{{c1::から::from}}五時{{c2::まで::until}}学校にいます。
tr: I'm at school from nine until five.
notes: から = from (time or place); まで = until / as far as.
tip: This から (from) differs from clause + から (because, unit 08).

text: 東京{{c1::から::from (place)}}来ました。
tr: I came from Tokyo.
notes: から = from (time or place); まで = until / as far as.
tip: This から (from) differs from clause + から (because, unit 08).

text: うちから学校{{c1::まで::to / as far as}}十分です。
tr: It's ten minutes from home to school.
notes: から = from (time or place); まで = until / as far as.
tip: This から (from) differs from clause + から (because, unit 08).

text: 友だち{{c1::と::と or で?}}ごはんを食べます。
tr: I eat with a friend.
notes: Person + と: together with.
tip: vs で: で = means/tool, never a companion.

text: 田中さん{{c1::と::と or で?}}日本へ行きました。
tr: I went to Japan with Mr Tanaka.
notes: Person + と: together with.
tip: vs で: で = means/tool, never a companion.

text:
(Only those two) つくえの上に本{{c1::と::と or や?}}ペンがあります。
(Among other things) つくえの上に本{{c2::や::と or や?}}ペンがあります。
tr: There's a book and a pen on the desk (nothing else). / There are a book, a pen and other things on the desk.
notes: と lists everything ('A and B'); や lists examples ('A, B and so on').
tip: と = complete list; や = non-exhaustive.

text: (Answering 'Who came?') 田中さん{{c1::が::は or が?}}来ました。
tr: Mr Tanaka came.
notes: は = topic already in the conversation; が = new information, or the answer to a question word.
tip: A question word as subject takes が (だれが来ましたか), and so does its answer.

text: (Asked 'What about Tanaka?') 田中さん{{c1::は::は or が?}}来ました。
tr: Tanaka? He came.
notes: は = topic already in the conversation; が = new information, or the answer to a question word.
tip: A question word as subject takes が (だれが来ましたか), and so does its answer.

text: (Spotting it suddenly) あ、ねこ{{c1::が::は or が?}}います。
tr: Oh, there's a cat.
notes: は = topic already in the conversation; が = new information, or the answer to a question word.
tip: A question word as subject takes が (だれが来ましたか), and so does its answer.

text:
つくえの上に本が{{c1::あります::あります or います?}}。
へやに犬が{{c2::います::あります or います?}}。
学校の前に木が{{c3::あります::あります or います?}}。
tr: There's a book on the desk. / There's a dog in the room. / There's a tree in front of the school.
notes: あります: things, plants, events. います: people and animals. Pattern: Place に Subject が あります/います.
tip: ある/いる are the plain forms.

text: 私は友だちが二人{{c1::います::あります or います?}}。
tr: I have two friends.
notes: あります: things, plants, events. います: people and animals. Pattern: Place に Subject が あります/います.
tip: ある/いる are the plain forms.

text: へやにだれも{{c1::いません::いる · polite negative}}。
tr: There's nobody in the room.
notes: あります: things, plants, events. います: people and animals. Pattern: Place に Subject が あります/います.
tip: ある/いる are the plain forms.

text: この本は{{c1::高くないです::高い · negative}}。
tr: This book isn't expensive.
notes: い-adj: drop い, add くないです. Exception: いい → よくない.

text: 今日は{{c1::いそがしくないです::いそがしい · negative}}。
tr: I'm not busy today.
notes: い-adj: drop い, add くないです. Exception: いい → よくない.

text: このへやは{{c1::大きくないです::大きい · negative}}。
tr: This room isn't big.
notes: い-adj: drop い, add くないです. Exception: いい → よくない.

text: てんきは{{c1::よくないです::いい · negative (irregular)}}。
tr: The weather isn't good.
notes: い-adj: drop い, add くないです. Exception: いい → よくない.

text: その店は{{c1::安かったです::安い · past}}。
tr: That shop was cheap.
notes: い-adj: drop い, add かったです (past) / くなかったです (past negative). いい → よかった.

text: この本は{{c1::おもしろかったです::おもしろい · past}}。
tr: This book was interesting.
notes: い-adj: drop い, add かったです (past) / くなかったです (past negative). いい → よかった.

text: 昨日のてんきは{{c1::よくなかったです::いい · past negative}}。
tr: Yesterday's weather wasn't good.
notes: い-adj: drop い, add かったです (past) / くなかったです (past negative). いい → よかった.

text: ごはんは{{c1::おいしくなかったです::おいしい · past negative}}。
tr: The meal wasn't tasty.
notes: い-adj: drop い, add かったです (past) / くなかったです (past negative). いい → よかった.

text: {{c1::きれいな::きれい · before a noun}}花です。
tr: It's a pretty flower.
notes: な-adj + な + noun. As a predicate it behaves like a noun: です, じゃありません, でした (no な).
tip: vs い-adj: い-adj go straight before nouns and conjugate themselves.

text: ここは{{c1::しずかな::しずか · before noun}}ところです。
tr: This is a quiet place.
notes: な-adj + な + noun. As a predicate it behaves like a noun: です, じゃありません, でした (no な).
tip: vs い-adj: い-adj go straight before nouns and conjugate themselves.

text: 私のへやは{{c1::きれいじゃありません::きれい · polite negative}}。
tr: My room isn't clean.
notes: な-adj + な + noun. As a predicate it behaves like a noun: です, じゃありません, でした (no な).
tip: vs い-adj: い-adj go straight before nouns and conjugate themselves.

text: 先生は{{c1::元気でした::元気 · polite past}}。
tr: The teacher was well.
notes: な-adj + な + noun. As a predicate it behaves like a noun: です, じゃありません, でした (no な).
tip: vs い-adj: い-adj go straight before nouns and conjugate themselves.

text: この店は{{c1::安くて::安い · て-form}}、おいしいです。
tr: This place is cheap and the food is good.
notes: い-adj: drop い + くて. な-adj / noun: + で. Links two descriptions ('and').

text: 田中さんは{{c1::しんせつで::しんせつ · て-form}}、おもしろい人です。
tr: Mr Tanaka is kind and fun.
notes: い-adj: drop い + くて. な-adj / noun: + で. Links two descriptions ('and').

text: このへやは{{c1::広くて::広い · て-form}}、明るいです。
tr: This room is spacious and bright.
notes: い-adj: drop い + くて. な-adj / noun: + で. Links two descriptions ('and').

text: 私は日本語{{c1::が::が or を?}}好きです。
tr: I like Japanese.
notes: These are な-adjectives. The thing liked or the skill takes が, not を.
tip: vs を: を is for action verbs.

text: おとうとはさかな{{c1::が::が or を?}}きらいです。
tr: My younger brother dislikes fish.
notes: These are な-adjectives. The thing liked or the skill takes が, not を.
tip: vs を: を is for action verbs.

text: 田中さんは日本語{{c1::が::が or を?}}じょうずです。
tr: Mr Tanaka is good at Japanese.
notes: These are な-adjectives. The thing liked or the skill takes が, not を.
tip: vs を: を is for action verbs.

text: 私はうた{{c1::が::が or を?}}へたです。
tr: I'm bad at singing.
notes: These are な-adjectives. The thing liked or the skill takes が, not を.
tip: vs を: を is for action verbs.

text: もうすぐ{{c1::春になります::春 · become}}。
tr: It will soon be spring.
notes: い-adj: drop い + くなる. な-adj and noun: + になる. 'Become'.

text: ふゆは{{c1::さむくなります::さむい · become}}。
tr: It gets cold in winter.
notes: い-adj: drop い + くなる. な-adj and noun: + になる. 'Become'.

text: 日本語が{{c1::じょうずになりました::じょうず · became}}。
tr: My Japanese has got better.
notes: い-adj: drop い + くなる. な-adj and noun: + になる. 'Become'.

text: ちょっと{{c1::待って::待つ · て-form}}ください。
tr: Please wait a moment.
notes: て-form: る-verb drop る+て (食べて); う/つ/る → って; む/ぶ/ぬ → んで; く → いて (行く → 行って is irregular); ぐ → いで; す → して; 来る → 来て; する → して. 〜てください = polite request.
tip: vs 〜ないでください: please don't.

text: ここに名前を{{c1::書いて::書く · て-form}}ください。
tr: Please write your name here.
notes: て-form: る-verb drop る+て (食べて); う/つ/る → って; む/ぶ/ぬ → んで; く → いて (行く → 行って is irregular); ぐ → いで; す → して; 来る → 来て; する → して. 〜てください = polite request.
tip: vs 〜ないでください: please don't.

text: 水を{{c1::飲んで::飲む · て-form}}ください。
tr: Please drink some water.
notes: て-form: る-verb drop る+て (食べて); う/つ/る → って; む/ぶ/ぬ → んで; く → いて (行く → 行って is irregular); ぐ → いで; す → して; 来る → 来て; する → して. 〜てください = polite request.
tip: vs 〜ないでください: please don't.

text: もう一度{{c1::言って::言う · て-form}}ください。
tr: Please say that once more.
notes: て-form: る-verb drop る+て (食べて); う/つ/る → って; む/ぶ/ぬ → んで; く → いて (行く → 行って is irregular); ぐ → いで; す → して; 来る → 来て; する → して. 〜てください = polite request.
tip: vs 〜ないでください: please don't.

text: 明日、早く{{c1::来て::来る · て-form}}ください。
tr: Please come early tomorrow.
notes: て-form: る-verb drop る+て (食べて); う/つ/る → って; む/ぶ/ぬ → んで; く → いて (行く → 行って is irregular); ぐ → いで; す → して; 来る → 来て; する → して. 〜てください = polite request.
tip: vs 〜ないでください: please don't.

text: ここで{{c1::食べないで::食べる · please don't}}ください。
tr: Please don't eat here.
notes: Plain negative (ない) + で + ください: 'please don't'.

text: しゃしんを{{c1::とらないで::とる · please don't}}ください。
tr: Please don't take photos.
notes: Plain negative (ない) + で + ください: 'please don't'.

text: {{c1::行かないで::行く · please don't}}ください。
tr: Please don't go.
notes: Plain negative (ない) + で + ください: 'please don't'.

text: 今、本を{{c1::読んでいます::読む · doing now}}。
tr: I'm reading a book now.
notes: て-form + います: an ongoing action, or a resulting state (すんでいます = live in).

text: 田中さんは今、ごはんを{{c1::食べています::食べる · doing now}}。
tr: Mr Tanaka is eating now.
notes: て-form + います: an ongoing action, or a resulting state (すんでいます = live in).

text: 私は東京に{{c1::すんでいます::すむ · live (ongoing state)}}。
tr: I live in Tokyo.
notes: て-form + います: an ongoing action, or a resulting state (すんでいます = live in).

text: ごはんを{{c1::食べてから::食べる · after doing}}、べんきょうします。
tr: After I eat, I study.
notes: て-form + から: after doing V. The first action is finished before the second starts.
tip: vs 〜前に: before (unit 07).

text: うちに{{c1::帰ってから::帰る · after doing}}、シャワーをあびます。
tr: After I get home, I take a shower.
notes: て-form + から: after doing V. The first action is finished before the second starts.
tip: vs 〜前に: before (unit 07).

text: 毎日、朝ごはんを食べて{{c1::から::after}}、学校へ行きます。
tr: Every day I go to school after eating breakfast.
notes: て-form + から: after doing V. The first action is finished before the second starts.
tip: vs 〜前に: before (unit 07).

text: 朝{{c1::起きて::起きる · て-form}}、かおをあらいます。
tr: I get up in the morning and wash my face.
notes: て-form links actions in order: 'do A, and then B'.

text: デパートへ{{c1::行って::行く · て-form}}、くつを買いました。
tr: I went to the department store and bought shoes.
notes: て-form links actions in order: 'do A, and then B'.

text: ここでしゃしんを{{c1::とってもいいですか::とる · may I?}}。
tr: May I take photos here?
notes: 〜てもいいです: permission. 〜てはいけません: prohibition.

text: ここでたばこを{{c1::すってはいけません::すう · must not}}。
tr: You must not smoke here.
notes: 〜てもいいです: permission. 〜てはいけません: prohibition.

text: ここに{{c1::すわってもいいです::すわる · may}}よ。
tr: You can sit here.
notes: 〜てもいいです: permission. 〜てはいけません: prohibition.

text: 私は肉を{{c1::食べない::食べる · plain negative}}。
tr: I don't eat meat.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::07 Plain forms and purpose
text: 明日は学校へ{{c1::行かない::行く · plain negative}}。

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::07 Plain forms and purpose
text: 田中さんは{{c1::来ない::来る · plain negative}}。
tr: Mr Tanaka isn't coming.
notes: う-verb: change the final u to a + ない (買う→買わない). る-verb: drop る + ない. 来る→来ない; する→しない; ある→ない.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::07 Plain forms and purpose
text: 今日は何も{{c1::しない::する · plain negative}}。
tr: I'm not doing anything today.
notes: う-verb: change the final u to a + ない (買う→買わない). る-verb: drop る + ない. 来る→来ない; する→しない; ある→ない.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::07 Plain forms and purpose
text: 昨日、友だちに{{c1::会った::会う · plain past}}。
tr: I met a friend yesterday.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::07 Plain forms and purpose
text: 朝ごはんを{{c1::食べた::食べる · plain past}}。
tr: I ate breakfast.
notes: Same sound changes as the て-form, with た/だ: 会った, 食べた, 読んだ, 行った (irregular).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::07 Plain forms and purpose
text: 本を{{c1::読んだ::読む · plain past}}。
tr: I read a book.
notes: Same sound changes as the て-form, with た/だ: 会った, 食べた, 読んだ, 行った (irregular).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::07 Plain forms and purpose
text: 学校に{{c1::行った::行く · plain past (irregular)}}。
tr: I went to school.
notes: Same sound changes as the て-form, with た/だ: 会った, 食べた, 読んだ, 行った (irregular).

text: ねる{{c1::前に::before}}、はをみがきます。

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::07 Plain forms and purpose
text: ごはんの{{c1::前に::before}}、手をあらいます。
tr: I wash my hands before meals.
notes: Dictionary-form verb + 前に, or noun + の前に: 'before'.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::07 Plain forms and purpose
text: 日本へ{{c1::行く前に::行く · before}}、日本語をべんきょうします。

text: デパートへ買い物{{c1::に::particle: in order to}}行きます。

text: としょかんへ本を{{c1::読みに::読む · in order to}}行きました。

tip: vs から (from): that one follows a time or place noun.
