text: (Asked 'Why did you take time off?') かぜ{{c1::ですから::because (polite)}}。
tr: Because I had a cold.
notes: Clause + から: 'because / so'. どうして asks why.
tip: vs から (from): that one follows a time or place noun.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: {{c1::どうして::why}}休みましたか。
tr: Why did you take time off?
notes: Clause + から: 'because / so'. どうして asks why.
tip: vs から (from): that one follows a time or place noun.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 日本語はむずかしいです{{c1::が::but}}、おもしろいです。
tr: Japanese is difficult, but interesting.
notes: Clause + が: 'but' (mild contrast).
tip: vs subject が (unit 04): this が follows a full clause.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: この店は高いです{{c1::が::but}}、おいしいです。
tr: This place is expensive, but the food is good.
notes: Clause + が: 'but' (mild contrast).
tip: vs subject が (unit 04): this が follows a full clause.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: この店は安いです。{{c1::そして::そして or それから?}}、おいしいです。
tr: This place is cheap. And the food is good.
notes: そして = and (also); それから = and then (next in time).
tip: Both start a new sentence; て-form links within one sentence.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: ごはんを食べました。{{c1::それから::そして or それから?}}、テレビを見ました。
tr: I ate. Then I watched TV.
notes: そして = and (also); それから = and then (next in time).
tip: Both start a new sentence; て-form links within one sentence.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 電車はバス{{c1::より::than}}はやいです。
tr: The train is faster than the bus.
notes: A は B より ~ = A is more ~ than B. A と B と どちらが? = which of two. A のほうが ~ = A is more ~. いちばん = most.
tip: どちら (two options) vs どれ (three or more).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: バスと電車と、{{c1::どちら::which}}が好きですか。
tr: Which do you like better, buses or trains?
notes: A は B より ~ = A is more ~ than B. A と B と どちらが? = which of two. A のほうが ~ = A is more ~. いちばん = most.
tip: どちら (two options) vs どれ (three or more).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 電車の{{c1::ほうが::more (of the two)}}はやいです。
tr: The train is faster.
notes: A は B より ~ = A is more ~ than B. A と B と どちらが? = which of two. A のほうが ~ = A is more ~. いちばん = most.
tip: どちら (two options) vs どれ (three or more).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 日本語が{{c1::いちばん::most}}好きです。
tr: I like Japanese the most.
notes: A は B より ~ = A is more ~ than B. A と B と どちらが? = which of two. A のほうが ~ = A is more ~. いちばん = most.
tip: どちら (two options) vs どれ (three or more).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 七時{{c1::ごろ::ごろ or ぐらい?}}起きます。
tr: I get up around seven.
notes: ごろ = around a point in time (clock time, date). ぐらい = about an amount or duration.
tip: ごろ = 'at about'; ぐらい = 'about how much / long'.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 毎日一時間{{c1::ぐらい::ごろ or ぐらい?}}べんきょうします。
tr: I study for about an hour every day.
notes: ごろ = around a point in time (clock time, date). ぐらい = about an amount or duration.
tip: ごろ = 'at about'; ぐらい = 'about how much / long'.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 水{{c1::だけ::only}}飲みます。
tr: I only drink water.
notes: Noun + だけ: only, just.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 学生は一人{{c1::だけ::only}}です。
tr: There is only one student.
notes: Noun + だけ: only, just.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 明日は雨{{c1::でしょう::probably (polite)}}。
tr: It will probably rain tomorrow.
notes: Plain form + でしょう: probably (prediction). With rising tone: 'right?'

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 田中さんは来る{{c1::でしょう::probably (polite)}}。
tr: Mr Tanaka will probably come.
notes: Plain form + でしょう: probably (prediction). With rising tone: 'right?'

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text:
(New info) 明日は休みです{{c1::よ::よ or ね?}}。
(Seeking agreement) いいてんきです{{c2::ね::よ or ね?}}。
tr: Tomorrow's a day off, you know. / Nice weather, isn't it?
notes: よ: telling the listener something they may not know. ね: seeking agreement ('isn't it?').

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: (Both of you eating) このごはん、おいしいです{{c1::ね::よ or ね?}}。
tr: This food is tasty, isn't it?
notes: よ: telling the listener something they may not know. ね: seeking agreement ('isn't it?').

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: (Telling a newcomer) あの人は先生です{{c1::よ::よ or ね?}}。
tr: That person is a teacher, you know.
notes: よ: telling the listener something they may not know. ね: seeking agreement ('isn't it?').

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 私は{{c1::あまり::not much}}おさけを飲みません。
tr: I don't drink alcohol much.
notes: あまり and ぜんぜん need a negative verb. よく and ときどき go with positive verbs.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 田中さんは{{c1::ぜんぜん::not at all}}日本語を話しません。
tr: Mr Tanaka doesn't speak Japanese at all.
notes: あまり and ぜんぜん need a negative verb. よく and ときどき go with positive verbs.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 友だちと{{c1::よく::often}}ごはんを食べます。
tr: I often eat with friends.
notes: あまり and ぜんぜん need a negative verb. よく and ときどき go with positive verbs.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: {{c1::ときどき::sometimes}}テレビを見ます。
tr: I sometimes watch TV.
notes: あまり and ぜんぜん need a negative verb. よく and ときどき go with positive verbs.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: (Asked 'Have you had lunch yet?') はい、{{c1::もう::already}}食べました。
tr: Yes, I've already eaten.
notes: もう + affirmative past = already. まだ + 〜ていません = not yet.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: (Asked 'Have you had lunch yet?') いいえ、{{c1::まだ::not yet}}食べていません。
tr: No, I haven't eaten yet.
notes: もう + affirmative past = already. まだ + 〜ていません = not yet.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: りんごを{{c1::ひとつ::1 + counter}}ください。
tr: One apple, please.
notes: つ-series for general items (ひとつ…とお). 人 for people (ひとり, ふたり are irregular). 冊 for bound items. 枚 for flat items.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 学生が{{c1::三人::3 + counter}}います。
tr: There are three students.
notes: つ-series for general items (ひとつ…とお). 人 for people (ひとり, ふたり are irregular). 冊 for bound items. 枚 for flat items.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 本を{{c1::二冊::2 + counter}}買いました。
tr: I bought two books.
notes: つ-series for general items (ひとつ…とお). 人 for people (ひとり, ふたり are irregular). 冊 for bound items. 枚 for flat items.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::N5::08 Connectors, comparison and extras
text: 紙を{{c1::三枚::3 + counter}}ください。
tr: Three sheets of paper, please.
notes: つ-series for general items (ひとつ…とお). 人 for people (ひとり, ふたり are irregular). 冊 for bound items. 枚 for flat items.

text: (Coach shouting) {{c1::走れ::走る · command (blunt)}}!
tr: Run!
notes: Imperative: う-verb: change the final u to e (走る → 走れ). る-verb: ろ (起きろ). する → しろ. 来る → 来い. Dictionary form + な: don't! Blunt: signs, sport, anger, orders being quoted.
tip: vs 〜なさい: firm but not rude. vs 〜てください: polite.

text: (Angry father) 早く{{c1::起きろ::起きる · command (blunt)}}!
tr: Get up!
notes: Imperative: う-verb: change the final u to e (走る → 走れ). る-verb: ろ (起きろ). する → しろ. 来る → 来い. Dictionary form + な: don't! Blunt: signs, sport, anger, orders being quoted.
tip: vs 〜なさい: firm but not rude. vs 〜てください: polite.

text: (A road sign) {{c1::止まれ::止まる · command (sign)}}。
tr: Stop.
notes: Imperative: う-verb: change the final u to e (走る → 走れ). る-verb: ろ (起きろ). する → しろ. 来る → 来い. Dictionary form + な: don't! Blunt: signs, sport, anger, orders being quoted.
tip: vs 〜なさい: firm but not rude. vs 〜てください: polite.

text: (A sign) ここに車を{{c1::止めるな::止める · don't! (blunt)}}。
tr: No parking here.
notes: Imperative: う-verb: change the final u to e (走る → 走れ). る-verb: ろ (起きろ). する → しろ. 来る → 来い. Dictionary form + な: don't! Blunt: signs, sport, anger, orders being quoted.
tip: vs 〜なさい: firm but not rude. vs 〜てください: polite.

text: (Mother to child) 早く{{c1::寝なさい::寝る · command (parent to child)}}。
tr: Go to bed now.
notes: Verb stem + なさい: do it (a parent or teacher to a child; firm but not rude).

text: (Teacher to students) 名前を{{c1::書きなさい::書く · command (teacher)}}。
tr: Write your names.
notes: Verb stem + なさい: do it (a parent or teacher to a child; firm but not rude).

text: 弟は新しいゲームを{{c1::ほしがっています::ほしい · (third person) wants}}。
tr: My little brother wants a new game.
notes: For a third person's feelings: い-adj without い + がる (ほしがる, こわがる); verb stem + たがる. Usually in ている form.
tip: vs ほしい / たい: only for yourself (or in questions to the listener).

text: 子どもは犬を{{c1::こわがっています::こわい · (third person) is scared of}}。
tr: The child is scared of the dog.
notes: For a third person's feelings: い-adj without い + がる (ほしがる, こわがる); verb stem + たがる. Usually in ている form.
tip: vs ほしい / たい: only for yourself (or in questions to the listener).

text: 妹はアメリカに{{c1::行きたがっています::行く · (third person) wants to}}。
tr: My little sister wants to go to America.
notes: For a third person's feelings: い-adj without い + がる (ほしがる, こわがる); verb stem + たがる. Usually in ている form.
tip: vs ほしい / たい: only for yourself (or in questions to the listener).

text: (Ordering) 私はコーヒー{{c1::にします::decide on / choose}}。
tr: I'll have a coffee.
notes: Noun + にする: decide on; choose (ordering, picking a date).

text: 旅行は来月{{c1::にしました::decided on}}。
tr: We've decided to go on the trip next month.
notes: Noun + にする: decide on; choose (ordering, picking a date).

text:
(You turned it up) テレビの音を{{c1::大きくしました::大きい · する or なる?}}。
(It got loud by itself) 急に音が{{c2::大きくなりました::大きい · する or なる?}}。
tr: I turned the TV up. / Suddenly the sound got loud.
notes: する: someone makes it so (い-adj → くする; な-adj / noun → にする). なる: it becomes so by itself.

text: 音を{{c1::小さくしてください::小さい · make (it)}}。
tr: Please turn the sound down.
notes: する: someone makes it so (い-adj → くする; な-adj / noun → にする). なる: it becomes so by itself.

text: へやを{{c1::きれいにしました::きれい · made (it)}}。
tr: I tidied the room.
notes: する: someone makes it so (い-adj → くする; な-adj / noun → にする). なる: it becomes so by itself.

text: もっと早く{{c1::来ればよかったです::来る · should have (regret)}}。
tr: I should have come earlier.
notes: ば-form + よかった: should have (regret). なければよかった: shouldn't have.
tip: たらよかった is also common.

text: かさを{{c1::持ってくればよかったです::持ってくる · should have (regret)}}。
tr: I should have brought an umbrella.
notes: ば-form + よかった: should have (regret). なければよかった: shouldn't have.
tip: たらよかった is also common.

text: あんなことを{{c1::言わなければよかったです::言う · shouldn't have}}。
tr: I shouldn't have said that.
notes: ば-form + よかった: should have (regret). なければよかった: shouldn't have.
tip: たらよかった is also common.

text: 少し{{c1::休んだらどうですか::休む · why don't you?}}。
tr: Why don't you rest a bit?
notes: Past た + らどうですか: why don't you? (suggestion). ば-form + いいですか: what should I do? (asking for advice).
tip: Asking a superior 'たらどうですか' can sound pushy.

text: どこで切符を{{c1::買えばいいですか::買う · where should I? (ば)}}。
tr: Where should I buy a ticket?
notes: Past た + らどうですか: why don't you? (suggestion). ば-form + いいですか: what should I do? (asking for advice).
tip: Asking a superior 'たらどうですか' can sound pushy.

text:
(Sometimes) ときどき会社まで{{c1::歩くことがあります::歩く · sometimes or have done?}}。
(Experience) 富士山に{{c2::登ったことがあります::登る · sometimes or have done?}}。
tr: I sometimes walk to work. / I have climbed Mount Fuji.
notes: Dictionary / ない form + ことがある: sometimes do. Past た + ことがある: have the experience of.

text: 忙しいときは、朝ごはんを{{c1::食べないことがあります::食べる · sometimes (not)}}。
tr: When I'm busy, I sometimes skip breakfast.
notes: Dictionary / ない form + ことがある: sometimes do. Past た + ことがある: have the experience of.

text: 会議は第一会議室{{c1::において::in / at (formal)}}行われます。
tr: The meeting will be held in Conference Room 1.
notes: Noun + において: in; at (formal 'で', for places, times, fields). における + noun.

text: 日本{{c1::における::in (+ noun, formal)}}外国人の数は増えています。
tr: The number of foreign residents in Japan is rising.
notes: Noun + において: in; at (formal 'で', for places, times, fields). における + noun.

text: 日本の文化{{c1::についての::about (+ noun)}}本を読みました。
tr: I read a book about Japanese culture.
notes: Before a noun: について → についての, に関して → に関する, に対して → に対する.

text: 環境問題{{c1::に関する::about (+ noun, formal)}}会議が開かれました。
tr: A conference on environmental issues was held.
notes: Before a noun: について → についての, に関して → に関する, に対して → に対する.

text: お客様{{c1::に対する::towards (+ noun)}}態度が悪いです。
tr: Their attitude towards customers is bad.
notes: Before a noun: について → についての, に関して → に関する, に対して → に対する.

text: 上に{{c1::行くにしたがって::行く · as (gradually)}}、気温が下がります。
tr: The higher you go, the lower the temperature.
notes: Dictionary form / noun + にしたがって: (a) as (gradually; slightly formal); (b) following (instructions).
tip: vs につれて: (a) means the same; only にしたがって has meaning (b).

text: 係員の指示{{c1::にしたがって::following (instructions)}}、避難してください。
tr: Please evacuate following the staff's instructions.
notes: Dictionary form / noun + にしたがって: (a) as (gradually; slightly formal); (b) following (instructions).
tip: vs につれて: (a) means the same; only にしたがって has meaning (b).

text: {{c1::焼きたて::焼く · freshly}}のパンはおいしいです。
tr: Freshly baked bread is delicious.
notes: Verb stem + たて: freshly (just made / just done).

text: {{c1::できたて::できる · freshly}}の料理をどうぞ。
tr: Please enjoy the food while it's fresh.
notes: Verb stem + たて: freshly (just made / just done).

text: この写真を{{c1::見るにつけ::見る · whenever (feelings arise)}}、昔を思い出します。
tr: Whenever I see this photo, it reminds me of the old days.
notes: Dictionary form + につけ: whenever (it brings up a feeling). 何かにつけ: at every opportunity.
tip: vs たびに: neutral 'every time'; につけ is about feelings.

text: 彼は何か{{c1::につけ::at every opportunity}}、文句を言います。
tr: He complains at every opportunity.
notes: Dictionary form + につけ: whenever (it brings up a feeling). 何かにつけ: at every opportunity.
tip: vs たびに: neutral 'every time'; につけ is about feelings.

text: 集めたデータ{{c1::をもとに::using … as a basis}}、グラフを作りました。
tr: I made a graph from the data I collected.
notes: Noun + をもとに: using X as the basis / source material.
tip: vs に基づいて: grounded in (facts, rules); をもとに: built from (material). Often interchangeable.

text: 祖母の話{{c1::をもとに::using … as source material}}、小説を書きました。
tr: I wrote a novel based on my grandmother's stories.
notes: Noun + をもとに: using X as the basis / source material.
tip: vs に基づいて: grounded in (facts, rules); をもとに: built from (material). Often interchangeable.

text: 心{{c1::をこめて::with (feeling)}}、手紙を書きました。
tr: I wrote the letter from the heart.
notes: Noun + をこめて: with (putting feeling into it).

text: 感謝{{c1::をこめて::with (feeling)}}、プレゼントを贈ります。
tr: I'm giving this present with gratitude.
notes: Noun + をこめて: with (putting feeling into it).

text: 年齢{{c1::を問わず::regardless of}}、だれでも参加できます。
tr: Anyone can take part, regardless of age.
notes: Noun + を問わず: regardless of.
tip: vs にかかわらず: same meaning; を問わず is common in job ads and notices.

text: 経験の有無{{c1::を問わず::regardless of}}、応募できます。
tr: You can apply with or without experience.
notes: Noun + を問わず: regardless of.
tip: vs にかかわらず: same meaning; を問わず is common in job ads and notices.

text: ファンの声{{c1::にこたえて::in response to}}、追加公演が決まりました。
tr: In response to the fans, an extra show has been added.
notes: Noun + にこたえて: in response to (a request, expectations).

text: 期待{{c1::にこたえて::in response to}}、彼は優勝しました。
tr: He lived up to expectations and won.
notes: Noun + にこたえて: in response to (a request, expectations).

text: ベルが{{c1::鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに::鳴る · just as / barely}}、彼は教室を出ました。
tr: The bell had barely rung when he left the classroom.
notes: Dictionary form + か + ない form + かのうちに: just as; barely (B happens almost at the same time).

text: 有名な先生の{{c1::もとで::under (guidance)}}、ピアノを習いました。
tr: I learned the piano under a famous teacher.
notes: Noun + のもとで: under (someone's guidance, or certain conditions).

text: 厳しい条件の{{c1::もとで::under (conditions)}}、実験が行われました。
tr: The experiment was carried out under strict conditions.
notes: Noun + のもとで: under (someone's guidance, or certain conditions).

text: 病状は悪くなる{{c1::ばかりです::keeps (getting worse)}}。
tr: His condition just keeps getting worse.
notes: Dictionary form + ばかりだ: just keeps getting (worse).
tip: Same meaning as 一方だ.

text: 彼は病気{{c1::をおして::pushing through (despite)}}、会議に出席しました。
tr: Despite being ill, he attended the meeting.
notes: Noun + をおして: pushing through (illness, opposition); despite.

text: それは教師に{{c1::あるまじき::ある · unbecoming of}}行為です。
tr: That's conduct unbecoming of a teacher.
notes: Noun に + あるまじき + noun: unbecoming of; unacceptable for (someone in that role). Verb + べからざる + noun: that must not / cannot (欠くべからざる = indispensable).

text: 水は生活に{{c1::欠くべからざる::欠く · indispensable (cannot lack)}}ものです。
tr: Water is indispensable to life.
notes: Noun に + あるまじき + noun: unbecoming of; unacceptable for (someone in that role). Verb + べからざる + noun: that must not / cannot (欠くべからざる = indispensable).

text: 仕事{{c1::にかまけて::too wrapped up in}}、家族のことを忘れていました。
tr: I was so wrapped up in work that I neglected my family.
notes: Noun + にかまけて: being too wrapped up in X (and neglecting something else).

text: 大学教授{{c1::ともあろう::someone of (such standing)}}人が、こんなミスをするなんて。
tr: For a university professor, of all people, to make such a mistake…
notes: Noun + ともあろう + noun: someone of such standing (should know better).

text: うちの息子{{c1::ときたら::when it comes to (complaint)}}、毎日ゲームばかりしています。
tr: As for my son, all he does is play games.
notes: Noun + ときたら: when it comes to X (complaining).
tip: vs にかけては: praise; ときたら: complaint.

text: 一回{{c1::ならまだしも::would be acceptable, but}}、何度も遅刻するのは困ります。
tr: Once would be fine, but being late again and again is a problem.
notes: Noun + ならまだしも: X would be acceptable, but (this isn't).
tip: Close to ならいざしらず.

text: (Written) 簡単だ{{c1::と思いきや::I thought …, but (actually)}}、とても難しかった。
tr: I thought it would be easy, but it was really hard.
notes: Plain form + と思いきや: I thought…, but in fact (the opposite).

text: (Written) 雨がやんだ{{c1::と思いきや::I thought …, but (actually)}}、また降り出した。
tr: Just when I thought the rain had stopped, it started again.
notes: Plain form + と思いきや: I thought…, but in fact (the opposite).

text: 努力した{{c1::かいもなく::in vain, despite}}、試験に落ちてしまいました。
tr: Despite all my efforts, I failed the exam.
notes: Past た / noun + の + かいもなく: despite (the effort), in vain.

text: 看病の{{c1::かいもなく::in vain, despite}}、祖父は亡くなりました。
tr: Despite our care, my grandfather passed away.
notes: Past た / noun + の + かいもなく: despite (the effort), in vain.

text: (Written) 夢を{{c1::実現せんがため::実現する · in order to (literary)}}、彼は全てを捨てた。
tr: To realise his dream, he gave up everything.
notes: ない form without ない + んがため(に) (する → せんがため): in order to (literary, strong resolve).
tip: vs ために: the everyday form.

text: 先生がいないの{{c1::をいいことに::taking advantage of}}、学生たちは騒いでいました。
tr: Taking advantage of the teacher's absence, the students were making a racket.
notes: Noun / plain form + の + をいいことに: taking (unfair) advantage of.

text: 最新の技術{{c1::をもってしても::even with}}、この病気は治せません。
tr: Even with the latest technology, this disease can't be cured.
notes: Noun + をもってしても: even with (the best means), still not.

text: この事故は{{c1::起こるべくして::起こる · bound to (inevitably)}}起こったものです。
tr: This accident was bound to happen.
notes: Verb + べくして + same verb: as was bound to happen (inevitably).

text: (Written) 彼は自分が天才だと{{c1::言ってはばからない::言う · not hesitate to}}。
tr: He openly claims to be a genius.
notes: て-form + はばからない: not hesitate to (say openly, often brazenly).

text: 借金を{{c1::してまで::する · go so far as to}}、車を買いたくはありません。
tr: I don't want to buy a car if it means going into debt.
notes: て-form + まで: go so far as to (do something extreme).

text: 私{{c1::とて::even (literary)}}、悲しくないわけではありません。
tr: Even I am not without sadness.
notes: Noun + とて: even (X, like everyone else; literary).
tip: vs でも / だって: the everyday forms.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::01 Transitive and intransitive pairs
text:
ドアが{{c1::あきました::あく or あける? (past)}}。
私がドアを{{c1::あけました::あく or あける? (past)}}。
tr: The door opened. / I opened the door.
notes: Intransitive verb + が: it happens (by itself). Transitive verb + を: someone does it to something.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::01 Transitive and intransitive pairs
text:
授業が九時に{{c1::始まります::始まる or 始める?}}。
先生が授業を{{c2::始めます::始まる or 始める?}}。
tr: Class starts at nine. / The teacher starts the class.
notes: Intransitive verb + が: it happens (by itself). Transitive verb + を: someone does it to something.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::01 Transitive and intransitive pairs
text:
電気が{{c1::つきました::つく or つける? (past)}}。
電気を{{c2::つけてください::つく or つける? (please)}}。
tr: The light came on. / Please turn on the light.
notes: Intransitive verb + が: it happens (by itself). Transitive verb + を: someone does it to something.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::01 Transitive and intransitive pairs
text:
コップが{{c1::落ちました::落ちる or 落とす? (past)}}。
コップを{{c2::落としました::落ちる or 落とす? (past)}}。
tr: The glass fell. / I dropped the glass.
notes: Intransitive verb + が: it happens (by itself). Transitive verb + を: someone does it to something.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::01 Transitive and intransitive pairs
text:
パソコンが{{c1::こわれました::こわれる or こわす? (past)}}。
弟がパソコンを{{c2::こわしました::こわれる or こわす? (past)}}。
tr: The computer broke. / My brother broke the computer.
notes: Intransitive verb + が: it happens (by itself). Transitive verb + を: someone does it to something.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::01 Transitive and intransitive pairs
text:
子どもが{{c1::起きました::起きる or 起こす? (past)}}。
母が子どもを{{c2::起こしました::起きる or 起こす? (past)}}。
tr: The child woke up. / The mother woke the child.
notes: Intransitive verb + が: it happens (by itself). Transitive verb + を: someone does it to something.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::01 Transitive and intransitive pairs
text:
車が{{c1::止まりました::止まる or 止める? (past)}}。
警察が車を{{c2::止めました::止まる or 止める? (past)}}。
tr: The car stopped. / The police stopped the car.
notes: Intransitive verb + が: it happens (by itself). Transitive verb + を: someone does it to something.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::01 Transitive and intransitive pairs
text:
お湯が{{c1::わきました::わく or わかす? (past)}}。
お湯を{{c2::わかしました::わく or わかす? (past)}}。
tr: The water has boiled. / I boiled some water.
notes: Intransitive verb + が: it happens (by itself). Transitive verb + を: someone does it to something.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::01 Transitive and intransitive pairs
text:
(It's just shut) 窓が{{c1::しまっています::しまる or しめる? (state)}}。
(Someone shut it on purpose) 窓が{{c2::しめてあります::しまる or しめる? (てある)}}。
tr: The window is shut. / The window has been shut (on purpose).
notes: Intransitive + ている: the state (no one implied). Transitive + てある: someone did it on purpose and the result remains.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::01 Transitive and intransitive pairs
text:
毎朝八時に家を{{c1::出ます::出る or 出す?}}。
毎朝ごみを{{c2::出します::出る or 出す?}}。
tr: I leave home at eight every morning. / I put the rubbish out every morning.
notes: Intransitive verb + が: it happens (by itself). Transitive verb + を: someone does it to something. Exception: with motion verbs like 出る, を marks the place you leave, not an object.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 姉は{{c1::結婚しています::結婚する · state (is married)}}。
tr: My older sister is married.
notes: With change-of-state verbs (結婚する, 来る, 行く, 勤める, 知る), ている means the resulting state, not 'is doing'. 知る: 知っています, but the negative is 知りません.
tip: vs action verbs (食べている): in progress.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 田中さんはもう{{c1::来ています::来る · state (is here)}}。
tr: Mr Tanaka is already here.
notes: With change-of-state verbs (結婚する, 来る, 行く, 勤める, 知る), ている means the resulting state, not 'is doing'. 知る: 知っています, but the negative is 知りません.
tip: vs action verbs (食べている): in progress.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 父は銀行に{{c1::勤めています::勤める · state (works at)}}。
tr: My father works at a bank.
notes: With change-of-state verbs (結婚する, 来る, 行く, 勤める, 知る), ている means the resulting state, not 'is doing'. 知る: 知っています, but the negative is 知りません.
tip: vs action verbs (食べている): in progress.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 「田中さんを知っていますか。」「いいえ、{{c1::知りません::知る · negative}}。」
tr: 'Do you know Mr Tanaka?' 'No, I don't.'
notes: With change-of-state verbs (結婚する, 来る, 行く, 勤める, 知る), ている means the resulting state, not 'is doing'. 知る: 知っています, but the negative is 知りません.
tip: vs action verbs (食べている): in progress.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text:
子どもたちが遊んでいる{{c1::の::の or こと?}}が見えます。
私の趣味は写真をとる{{c2::こと::の or こと?}}です。
tr: I can see the children playing. / My hobby is taking photos.
notes: の: something perceived or experienced directly (見る, 聞こえる, 手伝う, 待つ). こと: an abstract fact; required before です (趣味は〜ことです) and in ことができる / ことにする.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 田中さんが走っている{{c1::の::の or こと?}}を見ました。
tr: I saw Mr Tanaka running.
notes: の: something perceived or experienced directly (見る, 聞こえる, 手伝う, 待つ). こと: an abstract fact; required before です (趣味は〜ことです) and in ことができる / ことにする.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 日本語を話す{{c1::こと::の or こと?}}ができます。
tr: I can speak Japanese.
notes: の: something perceived or experienced directly (見る, 聞こえる, 手伝う, 待つ). こと: an abstract fact; required before です (趣味は〜ことです) and in ことができる / ことにする.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: お酒は飲みますが、たばこ{{c1::は::を or は?}}すいません。
tr: I drink, but I don't smoke.
notes: は after a noun (replacing を / が) or after another particle (には, では) marks contrast: 'X, at least / but not Y'.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 東京{{c1::には::に + contrast}}行きましたが、大阪には行きませんでした。
tr: I went to Tokyo, but not to Osaka.
notes: は after a noun (replacing を / が) or after another particle (には, では) marks contrast: 'X, at least / but not Y'.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 私{{c1::が::は or が?}}作ったケーキを食べてください。
tr: Please eat the cake I made.
notes: Inside a clause that modifies a noun or another clause (とき, から), the subject takes が, not は. は marks the topic of the whole sentence.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 母{{c1::が::は or が?}}帰ってきたとき、私は寝ていました。
tr: When my mother came home, I was asleep.
notes: Inside a clause that modifies a noun or another clause (とき, から), the subject takes が, not は. は marks the topic of the whole sentence.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text:
(You both went there) 去年行った{{c1::あの::その or あの?}}店、また行きたいね。
(Telling someone new) 駅の前に新しい店があって、{{c2::その::その or あの?}}店がとてもおいしいんです。
tr: I want to go back to that place we went last year. / There's a new place by the station, and it's really good.
notes: あの / あれ: something both speaker and listener know (shared memory). その / それ: something just mentioned that the listener doesn't know.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 毎朝、花に水を{{c1::やります::give (to plants)}}。
tr: I water the flowers every morning.
notes: やる: give (to plants, animals, or people below you). あげる is increasingly used for pets and plants too.
register: Casual; やる to people sounds rough

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 犬にえさを{{c1::やりました::give (to animals)}}。
tr: I fed the dog.
notes: やる: give (to plants, animals, or people below you). あげる is increasingly used for pets and plants too.
register: Casual; やる to people sounds rough

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 道{{c1::を::particle: across (motion)}}渡るときは、気をつけてください。
tr: Be careful when you cross the road.
notes: With motion verbs, を marks the route (渡る, 歩く, 通る) or the place you leave (出る, 降りる). This is not an object.
tip: vs で: where an action happens.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 次の駅で電車{{c1::を::particle: out of (getting off)}}降ります。
tr: I'm getting off the train at the next station.
notes: With motion verbs, を marks the route (渡る, 歩く, 通る) or the place you leave (出る, 降りる). This is not an object.
tip: vs で: where an action happens.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::02 Aspect, nominalisers and particles
text: 毎朝、八時に家{{c1::を::particle: out of (leaving)}}出ます。
tr: I leave home at eight every morning.
notes: With motion verbs, を marks the route (渡る, 歩く, 通る) or the place you leave (出る, 降りる). This is not an object.
tip: vs で: where an action happens.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) 今、何{{c1::してる::する · ている (casual)}}?
tr: What are you doing?
notes: In casual speech ている shortens to てる (ていた → てた).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) それ、もう{{c1::知ってる::知る · ている (casual)}}よ。
tr: I already know that.
notes: In casual speech ている shortens to てる (ていた → てた).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) 飲み物、{{c1::買っとく::買う · ておく (casual)}}ね。
tr: I'll get drinks in.
notes: ておく shortens to とく (でおく → どく).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) この本、ここに{{c1::置いとく::置く · ておく (casual)}}よ。
tr: I'll leave this book here.
notes: ておく shortens to とく (でおく → どく).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) ジュース、全部{{c1::飲んじゃった::飲む · てしまう (casual, past)}}。
tr: I drank all the juice.
notes: てしまう → ちゃう; でしまう → じゃう (past: ちゃった / じゃった).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) 電車、もう{{c1::行っちゃった::行く · てしまう (casual, past)}}。
tr: The train's already gone.
notes: てしまう → ちゃう; でしまう → じゃう (past: ちゃった / じゃった).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a child) ここで{{c1::泳いじゃ::泳ぐ · ては (casual)}}だめだよ。
tr: You mustn't swim here.
notes: ては → ちゃ; では → じゃ. Most often in ちゃだめ / ちゃいけない (mustn't).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) {{c1::見ちゃ::見る · ては (casual)}}だめ!
tr: Don't look!
notes: ては → ちゃ; では → じゃ. Most often in ちゃだめ / ちゃいけない (mustn't).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) 宿題、{{c1::やらなくちゃ::やる · must (なくちゃ)}}。
tr: I've got to do my homework.
notes: なくては(いけない) → なくちゃ; なければ(ならない) → なきゃ. The ending is often dropped.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) もう{{c1::行かなきゃ::行く · must (なきゃ)}}。
tr: I have to go now.
notes: なくては(いけない) → なくちゃ; なければ(ならない) → なきゃ. The ending is often dropped.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) 何言ってるか{{c1::わかんない::わかる · negative (casual ん)}}。
tr: I don't get what you're saying.
notes: In casual speech, ら / る / れ before な or の often becomes ん: わからない → わかんない; つまらない → つまんない; するの → すんの.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) この映画、{{c1::つまんない::つまらない · casual (ん)}}。
tr: This film's boring.
notes: In casual speech, ら / る / れ before な or の often becomes ん: わからない → わかんない; つまらない → つまんない; するの → すんの.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) いい{{c1::じゃん::isn't it! (casual)}}!
tr: That's great!
notes: Sentence-final じゃん: isn't it / you know (casual assertion; originally Kanto).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) だから言った{{c1::じゃん::I told you (casual)}}。
tr: I told you so.
notes: Sentence-final じゃん: isn't it / you know (casual assertion; originally Kanto).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) 会議は何時だった{{c1::っけ::was it? (trying to remember)}}?
tr: What time was the meeting again?
notes: Plain form (often past) + っけ: was it…? (trying to remember). Polite: でしたっけ.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) あの人、名前なんだ{{c1::っけ::was it? (trying to remember)}}?
tr: What was that person's name again?
notes: Plain form (often past) + っけ: was it…? (trying to remember). Polite: でしたっけ.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) 田中さん、結婚する{{c1::んだって::I heard (casual)}}。
tr: I heard Tanaka's getting married.
notes: Plain form + んだって: I heard; apparently (casual hearsay).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) あの店、来月閉まる{{c1::んだって::I heard (casual)}}。
tr: Apparently that shop's closing next month.
notes: Plain form + んだって: I heard; apparently (casual hearsay).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (Junior to senior) {{c1::そうっす::そうです · casual polite (っす)}}ね。
tr: Yeah, that's right.
notes: っす: a casual です, used mainly by younger men to seniors (sports, part-time jobs).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (Junior to senior) {{c1::いいっす::いいです · casual polite (っす)}}よ。
tr: Sure, no problem.
notes: っす: a casual です, used mainly by younger men to seniors (sports, part-time jobs).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) どこに{{c1::行くの::行く · question (casual)}}?
tr: Where are you going?
notes: Plain form + の? (rising): a casual question, softer than plain form alone. Noun / な-adj + なの?

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::03 Casual speech and contractions
text: (To a friend) それ、{{c1::本当なの::本当 · question (casual)}}?
tr: Is that true?
notes: Plain form + の? (rising): a casual question, softer than plain form alone. Noun / な-adj + なの?

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (Thinking aloud) 明日は晴れる{{c1::かな::I wonder (casual)}}。
tr: I wonder if it'll be sunny tomorrow.
notes: かな: I wonder (thinking aloud; neutral). かしら: the same, but feminine and rather old-fashioned.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (Older woman, thinking aloud) 田中さん、来る{{c1::かしら::I wonder (feminine, older)}}。
tr: I wonder whether Mr Tanaka is coming.
notes: かな: I wonder (thinking aloud; neutral). かしら: the same, but feminine and rather old-fashioned.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (Warning) 危ない{{c1::ぞ::warning (masculine)}}!
tr: Look out!
notes: ぞ: strong assertion or warning (masculine). ぜ: casual 'come on' / assertion (masculine, a bit dated).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (To a mate) 行こう{{c1::ぜ::let's (masculine, casual)}}!
tr: Let's go!
notes: ぞ: strong assertion or warning (masculine). ぜ: casual 'come on' / assertion (masculine, a bit dated).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: 明日は休みです{{c1::よね::right? (checking)}}。
tr: Tomorrow's a day off, right?
notes: よね: right? (checking something you think is true).
tip: vs ね: seeks agreement; よね checks your own belief.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (To a friend) これ、田中さんの{{c1::だよね::is, right? (casual check)}}。
tr: This is Tanaka's, isn't it?
notes: よね: right? (checking something you think is true).
tip: vs ね: seeks agreement; よね checks your own belief.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (Child) だって、まだ眠い{{c1::もん::because (childish excuse)}}。
tr: But I'm still sleepy!
notes: Plain form + もん (もの): because (a childish or sulky excuse).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (Sulking) 知らなかったんだ{{c1::もん::because (sulky excuse)}}。
tr: Well, I didn't know!
notes: Plain form + もん (もの): because (a childish or sulky excuse).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (Man, casual) いい天気だ{{c1::な::isn't it (masculine)}}。
tr: Nice weather, isn't it?
notes: Sentence-final な: a masculine or self-directed ね (isn't it; I think).
register: Casual; masculine or talking to yourself

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (To yourself) 今日は疲れた{{c1::な::(to yourself)}}。
tr: I'm tired today.
notes: Sentence-final な: a masculine or self-directed ね (isn't it; I think).
register: Casual; masculine or talking to yourself

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (Feminine, older Tokyo style) まあ、すてきだ{{c1::わ::feminine softener}}。
tr: Oh, how lovely.
notes: わ: (a) Tokyo: a feminine softener (now mostly older speech or fiction). (b) Kansai: a neutral assertion used by everyone.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (Kansai, anyone) もう帰る{{c1::わ::assertion (Kansai)}}。
tr: I'm off home.
notes: わ: (a) Tokyo: a feminine softener (now mostly older speech or fiction). (b) Kansai: a neutral assertion used by everyone.

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (To a friend) だから{{c1::さ::filler / emphasis}}、もう一回やろうよ。
tr: So, like, let's try again.
notes: さ: casual emphasis or filler, at the end or in the middle of a sentence (masculine-leaning).

deck: Cloze Grammar::Japanese::Beyond JLPT::04 Sentence-final particles and speech style
text: (To a friend) 大丈夫だ{{c1::さ::reassuring emphasis}}。
tr: It'll be fine.
notes: さ: casual emphasis or filler, at the end or in the middle of a sentence (masculine-leaning).

text: (Shop staff) トイレは二階{{c1::でございます::です · very polite}}。
tr: The toilets are on the second floor.
notes: ある → ございます; です → でございます (very polite, staff to customers).

text: (Shop staff) こちらにメニューが{{c1::ございます::ある · very polite}}。
tr: The menu is here.
notes: ある → ございます; です → でございます (very polite, staff to customers).

text: 明日、御社に{{c1::伺います::行く · humble (business)}}。
tr: I'll visit your company tomorrow.
notes: 伺う (行く / 聞く), 拝見する (見る), 存じる (知る / 思う), 申し上げる (言う, to a superior), いただく (もらう / 食べる).
tip: vs N4 humble: まいる, いたす, もうす.

text: 資料を{{c1::拝見しました::見る · humble}}。
tr: I've looked at the materials.
notes: 伺う (行く / 聞く), 拝見する (見る), 存じる (知る / 思う), 申し上げる (言う, to a superior), いただく (もらう / 食べる).
tip: vs N4 humble: まいる, いたす, もうす.

text: その件は{{c1::存じております::知る · humble (ongoing)}}。
tr: I'm aware of that matter.
notes: 伺う (行く / 聞く), 拝見する (見る), 存じる (知る / 思う), 申し上げる (言う, to a superior), いただく (もらう / 食べる).
tip: vs N4 humble: まいる, いたす, もうす.

text: 社長に{{c1::申し上げます::言う · humble (to a superior)}}。
tr: I'll tell the president.
notes: 伺う (行く / 聞く), 拝見する (見る), 存じる (知る / 思う), 申し上げる (言う, to a superior), いただく (もらう / 食べる).
tip: vs N4 humble: まいる, いたす, もうす.

text: 社長は今、電話で{{c1::話していらっしゃいます::話す · ている (honorific)}}。
tr: The president is on the phone right now.
notes: ている for a superior: ていらっしゃる (or the slightly weaker ておられる).

text: 先生は東京に{{c1::住んでいらっしゃいます::住む · ている (honorific)}}。
tr: The teacher lives in Tokyo.
notes: ている for a superior: ていらっしゃる (or the slightly weaker ておられる).

text: 少々{{c1::お待ちください::待つ · please (honorific)}}。
tr: Please wait a moment.
notes: お + stem + ください (ご + kanji noun + ください): please (honorific request). ご〜いただく: humble 'receive the favour of'.

text: こちらに{{c1::ご記入ください::記入する · please (honorific)}}。
tr: Please fill this in.
notes: お + stem + ください (ご + kanji noun + ください): please (honorific request). ご〜いただく: humble 'receive the favour of'.

text: {{c1::ご利用いただき::利用する · humble (receiving)}}、ありがとうございます。
tr: Thank you for using our services.
notes: お + stem + ください (ご + kanji noun + ください): please (honorific request). ご〜いただく: humble 'receive the favour of'.

text: (To a client, about your boss Tanaka) {{c1::田中::田中 or 田中さん?}}はただいま席を{{c2::外しております::外す · humble or honorific?}}。
tr: Tanaka is away from his desk at the moment.
notes: To someone outside your company, your own colleagues and boss are 'inside': no さん or title, and humble verbs (おる, いたす), even for your boss.

text: 社長が{{c1::おっしゃいました::おっしゃいました or おっしゃられました?}}。
tr: The president said so.
notes: Don't stack two honorific forms: おっしゃる is already honorific, so おっしゃられる is double. Common in speech but considered incorrect.

text: 部長はもう{{c1::お帰りになりました::お帰りになりました or お帰りになられました?}}。
tr: The manager has already gone home.
notes: Don't stack two honorific forms: おっしゃる is already honorific, so おっしゃられる is double. Common in speech but considered incorrect.

text: (Essay) 日本は島国{{c1::である::copula (essay style)}}。
tr: Japan is an island nation.
notes: In essays and reports, だ → である; ではない; であった. です / ます are not used.

text: (Essay) これは簡単な問題{{c1::ではない::copula negative (essay style)}}。
tr: This is not a simple problem.
notes: In essays and reports, だ → である; ではない; であった. です / ます are not used.

text: (Essay) この結果は重要{{c1::であった::copula past (essay style)}}。
tr: This result was important.
notes: In essays and reports, だ → である; ではない; であった. です / ます are not used.

text: (Written) 駅まで{{c1::歩き::歩く · and (written, stem)}}、電車に乗った。
tr: I walked to the station and got on a train.
notes: In writing, a verb stem (起き), い-adj in く (広く), or negative ず (言わず) links clauses instead of て-forms.

text: (Written) 彼は何も{{c1::言わず::言う · without (written ず)}}、部屋を出た。
tr: He left the room without a word.
notes: In writing, a verb stem (起き), い-adj in く (広く), or negative ず (言わず) links clauses instead of て-forms.

text: (Written) 部屋は{{c1::広く::広い · and (written)}}、明るい。
tr: The room is spacious and bright.
notes: In writing, a verb stem (起き), い-adj in く (広く), or negative ず (言わず) links clauses instead of て-forms.

text: (Essay) 問題はここにある{{c1::のである::explanatory (essay style)}}。
tr: This is where the problem lies.
notes: Plain form + のである: the written version of のです (explaining; stressing a conclusion).

text: (Report) この薬には効果がある{{c1::とされている::is said / held (report)}}。
tr: This drug is said to be effective.
notes: Plain form + とされている: is said / held to be. と考えられる: is thought (impersonal, reports).

text: (Report) 原因は気温の上昇だ{{c1::と考えられる::is thought (report)}}。
tr: The cause is thought to be the rise in temperature.
notes: Plain form + とされている: is said / held to be. と考えられる: is thought (impersonal, reports).

text: (Essay) 彼は医者{{c1::であり::is … and (written)}}、作家でもある。
tr: He is a doctor and also a writer.
notes: Noun + であり: written 'is … and' (links two descriptions).

text: (Written) {{c1::見知らぬ::見知る · negative (classical ぬ)}}人に話しかけられた。
tr: A stranger spoke to me.
notes: ぬ: classical negative (= ない), surviving before nouns and in proverbs and set phrases (見知らぬ, 知らぬが仏).

text: (Proverb) 知ら{{c1::ぬ::negative (classical)}}が仏。
tr: Ignorance is bliss.
notes: ぬ: classical negative (= ない), surviving before nouns and in proverbs and set phrases (見知らぬ, 知らぬが仏).

text: {{c1::思わず::思う · without meaning to (ず)}}笑ってしまいました。
tr: I couldn't help laughing.
notes: ず: classical negative, alive in everyday fixed phrases: 思わず (without meaning to), 相変わらず (as ever), 少なからず (not a little).

text: 彼は{{c1::相変わらず::as ever (fixed ず form)}}元気です。
tr: He's as energetic as ever.
notes: ず: classical negative, alive in everyday fixed phrases: 思わず (without meaning to), 相変わらず (as ever), 少なからず (not a little).

text: (Written) これは{{c1::知られざる::知られる · negative + noun (ざる)}}名作です。
tr: This is a little-known masterpiece.
notes: ざる: classical negative before a noun (知られざる = unknown).

text: (A maxim) 学生は勉強す{{c1::べし::must (classical)}}。
tr: Students must study.
notes: べし: must; should (classical root of べき; maxims, rules). ごとし: is like (classical root of ごとく).

text: (Proverb) 過ぎたるは猶及ばざるが{{c1::ごとし::is like (classical)}}。
tr: Too much is as bad as too little.
notes: べし: must; should (classical root of べき; maxims, rules). ごとし: is like (classical root of ごとく).

text: 彼は{{c1::堂々と::堂々 · adverb (と)}}意見を述べました。
tr: He stated his opinion confidently.
notes: A small set of Chinese-origin words (堂々, 確固, 漠然) take たる before nouns and と as adverbs.

text: それは{{c1::堂々たる::堂々 · before a noun (たる)}}演技でした。
tr: It was a commanding performance.
notes: A small set of Chinese-origin words (堂々, 確固, 漠然) take たる before nouns and と as adverbs.

text: (Motto) 失敗を恐れる{{c1::なかれ::do not (literary)}}。
tr: Do not fear failure.
notes: Dictionary form + なかれ: do not (literary command; mottos).

text: これは{{c1::若かりし::若い · past, before noun (classical)}}頃の写真です。
tr: This is a photo from my younger days.
notes: い-adj + かりし + noun: classical past (若かりし頃 = in my younger days).

text: (Kansai) 今日は{{c1::行かへん::行く · negative (Kansai)}}。
tr: I'm not going today.
notes: Kansai negative: ない → へん (行かない → 行かへん; 食べない → 食べへん). ん (行かん) is also common.

text: (Kansai) そんなん{{c1::知らへん::知る · negative (Kansai)}}。
tr: I don't know about that.
notes: Kansai negative: ない → へん (行かない → 行かへん; 食べない → 食べへん). ん (行かん) is also common.

text: (Kansai) それ、ほんま{{c1::や::copula だ (Kansai)}}。
tr: That's true.
notes: Kansai copula: だ → や (やで, やな, やろ).

text: (Kansai) 明日は雨{{c1::やで::copula + 'you know' (Kansai)}}。
tr: It's going to rain tomorrow, you know.
notes: Kansai copula: だ → や (やで, やな, やろ).

text: (Kansai) 今から帰る{{c1::ねん::explanatory んだ (Kansai)}}。
tr: I'm heading home now, see.
notes: Kansai explanatory ねん = んだ / のだ (noun / な-adj + やねん; past + ん + ねん → てん).

text: (Kansai) あの店、めっちゃ好き{{c1::やねん::copula + explanatory (Kansai)}}。
tr: I really love that place.
notes: Kansai explanatory ねん = んだ / のだ (noun / な-adj + やねん; past + ん + ねん → てん).

text: (Kansai) 先生、もう{{c1::帰らはった::帰る · light honorific, past (Kansai)}}。
tr: The teacher has already gone home.
notes: Kansai light honorific: verb stem (a-row for う-verbs) + はる. Used for respected people, and even for strangers.

text: (Kansai) あの人、何て{{c1::言わはった::言う · light honorific, past (Kansai)}}?
tr: What did that person say?
notes: Kansai light honorific: verb stem (a-row for う-verbs) + はる. Used for respected people, and even for strangers.

text: (Kansai) そんなことしたら{{c1::あかん::no good / mustn't (Kansai)}}。
tr: You mustn't do that.
notes: あかん = だめ (no good; mustn't). なあかん = なければならない (must).

text: (Kansai) もう{{c1::行かなあかん::行く · must (Kansai)}}。
tr: I've got to go.
notes: あかん = だめ (no good; mustn't). なあかん = なければならない (must).

text: (Kansai) 雨{{c1::やから::because (だから, Kansai)}}、家におるわ。
tr: It's raining, so I'll stay home.
notes: Kansai だから → やから.
